_note: Experiment 4 fixture freeze. Every web in "files" was authored BEFORE src/manyu/salience.py contained a selector, a threshold, or a loop - at freeze time the module held only TensionView, the fixture loader, and the digest helpers. Experiment 3 section 5 named the absence of this as one of the things standing between it and "done": its Stage 2 fixtures were written after the engine existed, so only negative_near_miss and the arm comparison were genuinely held out.
_enforcement: "files" is enforced continuously by verify_fixture_freeze - a fixture edit invalidates results. "standards" is enforced by verify_standards_freeze, which the RUNNER calls before a scored run and the test suite does not. Adding a criterion test strengthens the standard and should not require a re-freeze; weakening one after seeing a result is the actual risk, and that risk lives at the scored run. Re-freezing is an explicit act with a recorded reason.
_commit_note: Files were untracked at freeze time; the hashes here are the authority, not the commit.

mechanisms._mechanism_note: Recorded for the record only. This module is EXPECTED to change - the selector and loop are built on top of it. Not a mechanism freeze; that comes before the scored run, per experiment 2 FR-D3.2.

tests/test_salience_criteria.py.role: the criterion tests that make each fixture readable

tests/test_salience_substrate.py.role: what the substrate forces, pinned before any mechanism existed

tests/test_salience_mutants.py.role: the mutant battery that demonstrates the suite can catch defects

_standards_refreeze_note: Standards refreshed as the criterion tests, property tests and methodology landed. Still before any scored run - Stage 0a is void and Stages 2-4 ran only on authored webs - so there is no result a standard could have been weakened in response to.
_refreeze_reason: Re-frozen to add counter_direction and hub_web. Both were authored because the MUTANT BATTERY found the original seven could not catch two mutants, not because any result was visible - no scored run has happened. counter_direction separates "reads the direction off the graph" from "charges whichever side is weaker": on adversarial_grounding and aligned_grounding the declared target and the lower-staked party are the same belief, so the chosen_direction mutant - the exact motivated-reasoning behaviour Stage 4 exists to detect - passed every check. hub_web gives three conflicts a shared party so the ranking reorders after an action, without which a loop deciding from a stale reading is behaviourally identical to one re-reading each step. The original seven are byte-identical; nothing was weakened.
_refreeze_reason_2: Second re-freeze: added distractor_web and adversarial_multi. Stage 3 needs a web where some beliefs are unreachable from the conflict - on every earlier fixture every belief is reachable, so spread is 1.0 by construction and the measurement cannot fail. Stage 4 needs more than one conflict, because a single-conflict web cannot discriminate any ordering. Neither was authored in response to a result; no scored run has happened. The nine earlier webs are byte-identical.
